verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 56.43
verses.english: Linked Discourses 56.43

verses.pali: 5. Papātavagga
verses.english: 5. A Cliff

verses.pali: Mahāpariḷāhasutta
verses.english: The Great Scorching

verses.pali: “Atthi, bhikkhave, mahāpariḷāho nāma nirayo.
verses.english: “Mendicants, there is a hell called ‘The Great Scorching’.

verses.pali: Tattha yaṁ kiñci cakkhunā rūpaṁ passati, aniṭṭharūpaññeva passati no iṭṭharūpaṁ; akantarūpaññeva passati no kantarūpaṁ; amanāparūpaññeva passati no manāparūpaṁ.
verses.english: There, whatever sight you see with your eye is unlikable, not likable; undesirable, not desirable; unpleasant, not pleasant.

verses.pali: Yaṁ kiñci sotena saddaṁ suṇāti …pe…
verses.english: Whatever sound you hear … Whatever odor you smell … Whatever flavor you taste …

verses.pali: yaṁ kiñci kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṁ phusati …pe…
verses.english: Whatever touch you feel …

verses.pali: yaṁ kiñci manasā dhammaṁ vijānāti, aniṭṭharūpaññeva vijānāti no iṭṭharūpaṁ; akantarūpaññeva vijānāti no kantarūpaṁ; amanāparūpaññeva vijānāti no manāparūpan”ti.
verses.english: Whatever idea you know with your mind is unlikable, not likable; undesirable, not desirable; unpleasant, not pleasant.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha,

verses.pali: “mahā vata so, bhante, pariḷāho, sumahā vata so, bhante, pariḷāho.
verses.english: “Sir, that scorching really is mighty, so very mighty.

verses.pali: Atthi nu kho, bhante, etamhā pariḷāhā añño pariḷāho mahantataro ceva bhayānakataro cā”ti?
verses.english: Is there any other scorching more mighty and terrifying than this one?”

verses.pali: “Atthi kho, bhikkhu, etamhā pariḷāhā añño pariḷāho mahantataro ca bhayānakataro cā”ti.
verses.english: “There is, mendicant.”

verses.pali: “Katamo pana, bhante, etamhā pariḷāhā añño pariḷāho mahantataro ca bhayānakataro cā”ti?
verses.english: “But sir, what is it?”

verses.pali: “Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti …pe…
verses.english: “Mendicants, there are ascetics and brahmins who don’t truly understand about suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti, te jātisaṁvattanikesu saṅkhāresu abhiramanti …pe…
verses.english: They take pleasure in choices that lead to rebirth …

verses.pali: abhiratā …pe… abhisaṅkharonti …pe…
verses.english: They continue to make such choices …

verses.pali: abhisaṅkharitvā jātipariḷāhenapi pariḍayhanti, jarāpariḷāhenapi pariḍayhanti, maraṇapariḷāhenapi pariḍayhanti, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsapariḷāhenapi pariḍayhanti.
verses.english: Having made such choices, they burn with the scorching of rebirth, old age, and death, of sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

verses.pali: Te na parimuccanti jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi.
verses.english: They’re not freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

verses.pali: ‘Na parimuccanti dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: They’re not freed from suffering, I say.

verses.pali: Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti.
verses.english: There are ascetics and brahmins who truly understand about suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path.

verses.pali: Te jātisaṁvattanikesu saṅkhāresu nābhiramanti …pe…
verses.english: They don’t take pleasure in choices that lead to rebirth …

verses.pali: anabhiratā …pe… nābhisaṅkharonti …pe…
verses.english: They stop making such choices …

verses.pali: anabhisaṅkharitvā jātipariḷāhenapi na pariḍayhanti, jarāpariḷāhenapi na pariḍayhanti, maraṇapariḷāhenapi na pariḍayhanti, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsapariḷāhenapi na pariḍayhanti.
verses.english: Having stopped making such choices, they don’t burn with the scorching of rebirth, old age, and death, of sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

verses.pali: Te parimuccanti jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi.
verses.english: They’re freed from rebirth, old age, and death, from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.

verses.pali: ‘Parimuccanti dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
verses.english: They’re freed from suffering, I say.

verses.pali: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yogo karaṇīyo …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti.
verses.english: That’s why you should practice meditation …”

verses.pali: Tatiyaṁ.
